title: Your AI Receptionist Might Be Cheaper Than You Think (But Here's What Actually Matters)
excerpt: AI receptionists are getting real for small businesses, and the pricing might surprise you — but before you jump in, there's one thing you absolutely need to test.

content.text: So here's something that caught my eye today: AI receptionists are actually becoming a real option for small businesses now, not just some sci-fi thing on the horizon. And the money side is way less intimidating than it used to be. But — and this is important — pricing isn't the part you should be sweating about.

A few years ago, AI receptionists were either impossibly expensive or absolutely terrible at their job. You'd call and get stuck in a loop of "I didn't understand that, please repeat." Super frustrating, and honestly, bad for your business reputation. Now there are real options that actually handle calls like a human would — transferring to the right person, taking messages, scheduling appointments, the whole deal.

The pricing has gotten reasonable too. You're looking at somewhere in the ballpark of what you'd pay for a part-time receptionist's salary for a few hours a week, not thousands of dollars a month. Some options run on a pay-per-use model, some are flat monthly fees. Point is: it's not a financial cliff anymore.
The Thing Nobody Talks About: Call Quality

Here's where I need to be real with you. Just because the price is now doable doesn't mean every option sounds the same or works the same. Some AI receptionists sound natural. Some sound like they're reading off a script written in 2010. Some actually understand context and can handle weird customer requests. Some get confused and transfer people to the wrong department three times.
The biggest mistake small business owners make: they pick based on price or features without actually listening to how it sounds to a real person calling their business.
What You Actually Need to Do

items: Test-drive any option before you commit. Most companies let you try them, and you should. Call it. Have your team call it. Pretend you're a customer.
Listen for how it handles the weird stuff — transfers, hold times, when it doesn't understand something. Those moments matter way more than the easy calls.

Ask about integration with your actual phone system and CRM (that's your customer relationship management software, where you store client info). A great AI receptionist that can't talk to your other tools is just expensive and frustrating.
Think about what this actually solves for your business. Are you drowning in missed calls after hours? Do you need someone screening calls? Scheduling? Know that before you go shopping.

content.label: Intecha's Take
content.text: AI receptionists are worth looking at right now — the technology actually works and it's affordable. But do not let price be your main filter. Your customers are calling your business. Make sure whatever you pick sounds and acts like you actually care about that call. Test first, decide second. Your reputation is on the line, not your receptionist's.
